checked.found: Caesar arrived after Pompey's death, took sides in the Ptolemaic throne dispute and was besieged in the palace/Royal Quarter from late 48 BC (some sources Aug 48) into 47 BC. Year is the start of the siege; name and description supported.
Octavian took Egypt in 30 BC after Antony and Cleopatra's deaths; Egypt was treated as the emperor's personal possession.
Portuguese conquest of Ceuta, August 1415, widely given as the start of Portuguese overseas expansion (not searched this session beyond the spine source; well attested).
Fleet left Lisbon July 1497, rounded the Cape Nov 1497, reached Mozambique and Mombasa in early 1498. Year 1497 is the departure, as the deck notes. Description states no date.
Battle of Alcacer Quibir, 4 August 1578; King Sebastian killed, Aviz dynasty ended (not searched this session beyond the spine source; well attested).
Reached the Niger at Segou in July 1796 (verified earlier).
Battle of Blood River, 16 December 1838, Voortrekkers under Pretorius beat Zulu forces under Dingane at the Ncome River in Natal.
Livingstone reached Victoria Falls 16/17 November 1855 and named them for Queen Victoria. The 'paddling down the Zambezi' wording is consistent with his canoe journey.
British expedition to Abyssinia; Magdala stormed 13 April 1868 (Arogee 10 April); Tewodros II died by suicide; aim was freeing British captives.
Italy declared war 29 Sept 1911 and landed at Tripoli on 4-5 October 1911, with other ports taken soon after; Libya was an Ottoman possession.

Year 1912 is right (signed 30 March 1912, French protectorate). But sources conflict on whether the Spanish northern zone belongs to the Fez treaty itself; most put its legal basis in the separate Franco-Spanish Madrid treaty of 27 November 1912. Description's 'a northern zone left to Spain' is therefore loosely attributed to the treaty.
Battle of Annual, 21-22 July 1921; Abd el-Krim's Rif tribesmen routed a Spanish army, widely called Spain's worst colonial defeat.
